title: Civil Affairs Senior Sergeant (Active Component Only)
raw_text:
10-38Z. MOS 38Z--Civil Affairs Senior Sergeant (Active Component Only), CMF 38 (Effective
202410)
     a. Major duties. The Civil Affairs (CA) Senior Sergeant supervises, leads, or serves as a member of a
CA unit that executes CA missions in support of national security objectives or as a CA subject matter
expert in an Army or Joint Service organization. Duties of MOS 38Z at each level of skill are:
          (1) MOS 38Z4O. The CA Team Sergeant is the Master Trainer of a four-person, regionally
aligned Civil Affairs Team (CAT) responsible for ensuring the team is proficient in individual and collective
critical tasks. The CA Team Sergeant is overall responsible for providing tactical and technical guidance
and professional support to subordinates in accomplishing their duties. The CA Team Sergeant is the
principal advisor to the leadership in the tactical employment of the CAT in hostile, denied, or politically
sensitive environments through the utilization of specialized tactics, techniques, and procedures to
conduct civil reconnaissance, civil engagement, and civil network development to find, disrupt, and defeat
hybrid threats in the civil component. The key developmental position for MOS 38Z4O is a Team
Sergeant on a Civil Affairs Team.
          (2) MOSC 38Z5O.
              (a) MSG: Supervises the processing of operations and civil knowledge in a CA company or
higher-level unit. Provides tactical and technical guidance to subordinates and professional support to
both subordinates and superiors in accomplishment of their duties. Plans, coordinates, and supervises
activities pertaining to organization, training, and operations. Develops and reviews tactical plans and
training materials. Coordinates implementation of operations, training programs.
              (b) 1SG: Serves as Senior Enlisted Advisor to the Company Commander. 1SGs are
responsible for maintaining and enforcing standards, ensuring training objectives are met, developing the
Soldiers in the unit, all administrative functions, and ensuring the health, welfare, and morale of the unit
and their families. Responsible for enlisted manning and talent management, leader professional
development, and NCO Common Core Competencies. Provides tactical and technical guidance to
subordinates and professional support to both subordinates and superiors in accomplishment of their
duties. Plans, coordinates, and supervises activities pertaining to administration, training, and logistics for
the company. Supervises implementation of operations and training programs. The key developmental
position for MOS 38Z5O is First Sergeant in a Civil Affairs Company.
          (3) MOSC 38Z6O.
              (a) SGM: Serves as principal noncommissioned officer in a Civil Affairs battalion or higher to
the staff and Operations Officer. Leverages experience to supervise the processing of operations.
Provides tactical and technical guidance to subordinates and professional support to both subordinates
and superiors in accomplishment of their duties. Plans, coordinates, and supervises activities pertaining
to organization, training, and operations. Develops and reviews tactical plans and training materials at the
battalion and higher level. Coordinates implementation of operations and training programs. The SGM is
a subject matter expert in their field, primary advisor on policy development, analytical reviewer of
regulatory guidance and often fulfills the duties of the CSM in the incumbent’s absence.
              (b) CSM: Serves as Command Senior Enlisted Advisor to the Commander (Battalion and
higher-level unit) on all enlisted issues and is primarily focused on the training, maintaining, caring, and
leading of the unit's Soldiers, facilities, and equipment. Assists the Commander in the implementation of
command policies and establishes and enforces standards related to the appearance and conduct of all
Soldiers within the command. Develops and executes NCO Professional Development Programs within
the command and advises/counsels Soldiers on issues related to training, education, and professional
development. Responsible for the unit’s individual skills training program for all CMFs. (Battalion and
higher-level unit).
     b. Physical demands rating and qualification to maintain MOS. Civil Affairs Senior Sergeants must
possess the following qualifications:
          (1) A physical demands rating of Significant (Gray).
          (2) A physical profile of 111221.
          (3) A minimum score of 107 in aptitude area.
          (4) A minimum OPAT score of Long Jump (LJ) – 0120 cm, Seated Power Throw (PT) – 0350 cm,
Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0036 shuttles in Physical Demand
Category “Significant” (Gray).
          (5) Must be airborne qualified and maintain SQI P Parachutist.




                                                       1
           (6) Must be Survival, Evasion, Resistance, and Escape Level C (SERE-C) graduate effective on
and after 1 October 2024.
          (7) A minimum-security eligibility of SECRET is required for the initial award and to maintain the
MOS.
          (8) Eligible to obtain Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS-SCI) clearance in
accordance with AR 380–67.
          (9) A U.S. citizen or naturalized citizen.
          (10) High school graduate or GED certificate.
          (11) If awarded ASI W4, must maintain a current, valid, unrestricted National Registry Emergency
Medical Technician (NREMT) Certification and USSOCOM Advanced Tactical Paramedic (ATP)
Certification. 1SGs, SGMs, and CSMs are exempt from this requirement.
          (12) Not barred to reenlist IAW AR 601-280, or under suspension of favorable personnel action
IAW AR 600-8-2.
          (13) No history of a qualifying military or civilian conviction of a crime of domestic violence, as
defined by AR 600-20, Army Command Policy, paragraph 4-22.
          (14) No history of any use of an illicit substance following the Soldier's date of initial entry into
military service.
          (15) No history of any use of a controlled substance without a valid prescription following the
Soldier's date of initial entry into military service.
          (16) No history of a military or civilian charge for Driving Under the Influence or Reckless Driving.
          (17) No history of any other open military or civilian administrative or criminal investigation,
charge, or indictment on the Soldier
          (18) No record of conviction by special or general courts-martial or civilian courts of offenses
listed in AR 27-10 (Military Justice) chapter 24 or otherwise required to register as a sexual offender
under AR 27-10, chapter 24.
          (19) Reclassification. Must meet all prerequisites IAW 614-200 Ch 10.
    c. Additional skill identifiers: (Note: Refer to table 12-8 for (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
enlisted MOS)).
         (1) W4—Special Operations Civil Affairs Medical Sergeant.
         (2) J8—Government Support Element (GSE)
         (3) 6B—Reconnaissance and Surveillance Leaders Course (personnel only).
         (4) 8H-- Minimum MOS Qualified Master Sergeant (personnel only) (Effective 202408).
         (5) L8-- Joint Operational Fires and Effects (JOFE) (skill level 4 only; personnel and positions).
(Effective 202610)
 (Note: Refer to table 12-8 for (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all enlisted MOS)).
    d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to each skill
level are listed in the following tables:
          (1) Table 10-38Z-1. Physical requirements.
          (2) Table 10-38Z-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
          (3) Table 10-38Z-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
